ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the topmost part of the structure shown?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This image is a schematic cross-sectional diagram of plant leaf tissue. At the very top, a continuous row of yellow rectangular cells can be seen, located on the highest surface of the entire structure. Below it are green columnar and irregular tissue cells. Reasoning: The question asks what the uppermost part of this structure is. In a leaf cross-section, the cell layer located on the outermost side, at the very top, and serving a protective function is called the epidermis, specifically called the upper epidermis. Therefore the answer is epidermis.
